findings.finding: The word "selection" is overloaded across the two sources, and the documentary state carrying it is mis-attributed to the Figma source. docs/spec.md embeds STATE-1 with "origin": "FIGMA" and "disposition": "REQUIRED", yet the behaviour exists only in the markdown and is explicitly disclaimed there as "not a rendered chip selection". The materialized consumer manifest confirms the mis-attribution: STATE-1 is carried under the FIGMA reference (SRC-d2af03e3610e846a8ea56584, reference_hash 691e8f07...) while its document_ids resolve only to DOC = docs/spec.md. The same inconsistency is propagated into the atomicity contract: AST-09f364d3631a1a08151e7a46 has source = MARKDOWN/docs/spec.md but its figma_document_state block sets source_id to the FIGMA source and carries the Figma reference_hash. Meanwhile frame 4478:7209 genuinely does render a chip selection affordance in the frozen snapshot (component set 3302:4166, with 4953:6620 "Cuisses" and 4953:6625 "Fessier" instantiated as State=Selected, visible in zones-reference.png), and every one of those chip units is dispositioned CONTEXT_ONLY. A reader of the plan therefore sees a FIGMA-origin REQUIRED "selection" state attached to a frame whose Figma-observable selection is deliberately not realized. The narrowing is intentional and is carried as a residual risk, so this is not a blocking defect, but the provenance labelling currently asserts a Figma origin for an observable that was never observed in Figma.

findings.finding: The plan's evidence-deposit enumeration is narrower than what the VISUAL_COMPARE proofs require it to retain. Both PROOF-e88ba6e1b93425956c20f40a and PROOF-77d040e2e7bbc5cafae41136 state "Retain rendered.png, rendered.html and browser-facts.json at each viewport", but the implementation_constraints describe each review directory as containing only "rendered.png, browser-facts.json and independent-viewport/rendered.png plus independent-viewport/browser-facts.json" - rendered.html is omitted at both viewports. The observer in fact writes rendered.html at each viewport, so the artifact exists and the proof is satisfiable; the defect is in the plan text, not the mechanism. It still matters: rendered.html is the generated host whose SHA-256 must equal the loaded-document hash, so an auditor working only from the plan's declared deposit layout would not know that the artifact backing that equality check is retained and re-verifiable.

findings.finding: The declared boundary (forbidden_policy ALL_OUTSIDE_WRITE_SCOPE, constraint "Only the declared code and test paths may change") is not positioned to cover filesystem side effects produced while tests/ui.test.js runs. All three test obligations require the delivery to spawn isolated child Node processes ("Run the sentinel block once in an isolated child Node process", "In a separate isolated child Node process, load Screen freshly"), which materially raises the chance that an implementer writes temporary helper files to drive those subprocesses. In the orchestration that enforces the boundary, assertDelta - which is what checks `git diff --name-only HEAD` against [Screen.js, tests/ui.test.js] and asserts `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` is empty - runs strictly before the test is executed, on both the initial pass and the bounded correction pass. Any untracked artifact created during test execution is therefore never caught by the write-scope gate. The plan states the subprocess requirement but never constrains how the subprocess is to be launched, so the boundary it declares is weaker in practice than it reads.

planContract implementation_constraints: "Only the declared code and test paths may change" is stated but carries no constraint on test-runtime filesystem effects

findings.required_correction: Add an explicit implementation constraint that tests/ui.test.js must create no filesystem artifacts inside the checkout: the required isolated subprocesses must be launched with inline source (for example execFileSync(process.execPath, ['-e', ...])) and must not write temporary files or directories. Alternatively, require the write-scope assertion (changed-files plus untracked-files check) to be re-evaluated after test execution rather than only before it, so the declared ALL_OUTSIDE_WRITE_SCOPE boundary is actually enforced across the whole delivery.
